edges.description: Spores lodged in the damaged umbilical remnant encounter a nutrient-rich, devitalized bacterial growth niche.
Vegetative C. tetani secretes tetanus neurotoxin from the contaminated umbilical site.
Secreted toxin reaches peripheral cholinergic terminals and binds neonatal motor axons.
Internalized toxin traffics retrogradely from the umbilical infection site toward central motor circuits.
Tetanus toxin leaves motor neurons in the CNS and targets presynaptic GABAergic and glycinergic interneurons.
Loss of inhibitory neurotransmission disinhibits neonatal motor neurons.
Spastic neonatal oromotor dysfunction prevents effective breast feeding.
Masseter and jaw-muscle overactivity produces neonatal lock jaw.
Unchecked motor firing produces diffuse sustained rigidity.
Loss of inhibitory motor control produces painful generalized spasms.
Brainstem and respiratory-muscle involvement can produce apneic episodes.
Laryngeal and respiratory-muscle spasms can obstruct the airway or arrest breathing.
Nonsterile material applied directly to the umbilical cord can deliver environmental C. tetani spores into the devitalized stump.

nodes.description: Severe neonatal tetanus can interrupt breathing through brainstem and respiratory-muscle spasm.

evidence.reference_title: A review of 207 newborn with tetanus.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent cause of death was apnea in the first week and sepsis in the later period.

nodes.description: Hygienic delivery and cord care, with topical antimicrobials where neonatal tetanus risk is high, prevent hazardous spore introduction and early umbilical bacterial expansion.

evidence.reference_title: Protective effects of topical antimicrobials against neonatal tetanus.
evidence.snippet: Continuous use of antimicrobial agents (antibiotics and antiseptics) at delivery and during the first few days after delivery was highly protective in univariate testing (matched odds ratio 0.2 [95% confidence interval: 0.11-0.64], P = 0.003), and remained significantly protective when other delivery and cord care practices were controlled.

evidence.reference_title: Topical application of chlorhexidine to neonatal umbilical cords for prevention of omphalitis and neonatal mortality in a rural district of Pakistan: a community-based, cluster-randomised trial.
evidence.snippet: Application of 4% CHX to the umbilical cord was effective in reducing the risk of omphalitis and neonatal mortality in rural Pakistan.

nodes.description: The cut umbilical cord is devitalized tissue that supports bacterial colonization; in this niche, contaminating C. tetani spores can germinate into vegetative bacilli.

evidence.reference_title: Umbilical Cord Care in the Newborn Infant.
evidence.snippet: After birth, the devitalized umbilical cord often proves to be an ideal substrate for bacterial growth and also provides direct access to the bloodstream of the neonate.

nodes.description: Diffuse sustained muscle contraction produces whole-body neonatal rigidity.

evidence.snippet: C tetani releases a potent neurotoxin, causing muscle spasms, rigidity, and dysautonomia.

nodes.description: The tetanus light chain cleaves synaptobrevin-2, disrupts SNARE-dependent vesicle fusion, and prevents inhibitory GABA and glycine release onto motor neurons.

evidence.snippet: disrupting the SNARE complex essential for neurotransmitter release.

nodes.description: Tetanus toxoid vaccination before or during pregnancy induces maternal IgG that crosses the placenta and passively protects the newborn against umbilical tetanus.

evidence.snippet: antibodies are transmitted transplacentally and vaccinating girls therefore prevents neonatal tetanus.

nodes.description: Metronidazole or another anaerobic antibiotic suppresses vegetative C. tetani in the umbilical focus and prevents additional local tetanus-toxin secretion.

evidence.snippet: Enteral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics should be administered for 7-10 days.

nodes.description: Tetanus neurotoxin binds peripheral motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction and enters retrograde endosomal carriers.

evidence.snippet: TeNT binds to peripheral motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction and undergoes retrograde axonal transport to the spinal cord and brainstem, similar to the rabies virus.

nodes.description: Disinhibited motor firing produces impaired suckling, trismus, rigidity, painful spasms, apnea, and generalized neonatal tetanus.

evidence.snippet: The resultant failure of inhibitory neurotransmission leads to unchecked downstream motor activity, manifesting as muscle rigidity, spasms, and hyperreflexia.

nodes.description: Application of clay, animal dung, ash, or other nonsterile traditional substances to the cut umbilical cord can inoculate the neonatal stump with C. tetani spores.

evidence.snippet: The findings indicated that tetanus in a newborn of an unvaccinated mother occurred after application of nonsterile clay to the umbilical cord.

nodes.description: Neonatal tetanus commonly presents with inability to suck effectively after the toxin-mediated spastic syndrome begins.

evidence.reference_title: A review of 207 newborn with tetanus.
evidence.snippet: Failure to suck and twitching were the most frequent symptoms.

nodes.description: Toxin-mediated loss of inhibitory neurotransmission produces painful generalized spasms and twitching in neonatal tetanus.

evidence.reference_title: A review of 207 newborn with tetanus.
evidence.snippet: Failure to suck and twitching were the most frequent symptoms.

nodes.description: Airway obstruction, respiratory arrest, or recurrent apnea can lead to life-threatening respiratory failure.

evidence.snippet: Important complications include laryngeal spasm and resultant airway obstruction and respiratory arrest

nodes.description: Retrograde axonal transport delivers active tetanus toxin to the spinal cord and brainstem, where it can move trans-synaptically into inhibitory interneurons.

evidence.snippet: Within the CNS, TeNT targets presynaptic glycine- and GABA-ergic interneurons, cleaving its substrate, synaptobrevin-2

nodes.description: Tetanus immune globulin neutralizes unbound toxin before it binds and enters neonatal motor axon terminals.

evidence.snippet: Administration of antitoxin via an intramuscular (IM) or IV route improves mortality in tetanus.

nodes.description: Jaw-muscle spasm produces lock jaw in neonatal tetanus.

evidence.reference_title: Risk factors, morbidity and mortality of neonatal tetanus.
evidence.snippet: The retrospective study identified that mortality due to neonatal tetanus was very high and the common morbidities were lock jaw, inability to suck, abdominal rigidity, convulsion, fever, irritability etc.

nodes.description: Spores from nonsterile delivery or cord-care materials are introduced onto neonatal umbilical tissue after the cord is cut.

evidence.snippet: NT is associated with nonsterile delivery and umbilical cord-care practices for newborns of mothers with antitoxin levels insufficient to protect the newborn by transplacental transfer of maternal antibody.

nodes.description: Germinated C. tetani remains localized in the umbilical wound and secretes tetanus neurotoxin.

evidence.snippet: Once introduced, spores germinate, and bacilli secrete two key toxins: tetanolysin and TeNT.

nodes.description: Careful debridement or cleaning of infected umbilical tissue removes the devitalized anaerobic niche that supports additional C. tetani toxin secretion.

evidence.snippet: Surgical debridement is required to eradicate necrotic tissue that may harbour C. tetani, even for wounds that appear innocuous.
